Server._MaxConnections_note: Kept at (select FD_SETSIZE 1024 - FdReserve 64) so the shipped config is achievable: the broker clamps anything higher and logs the clamp, because select(2) cannot watch a descriptor at or above FD_SETSIZE.
Server._FdReserve_note: Descriptors held back from the connection budget for listeners, metrics, replication, and the log + timeindex file each open partition keeps. MaxConnections is clamped to (select FD_SETSIZE - FdReserve); raise this on a broker with many partitions.
Server._Tls_note: TLS for the client listener. Omit (the default) and the port stays plaintext, which is what every existing deployment gets on upgrade. { "CertFile": "/etc/moonmq/server.crt", "KeyFile": "/etc/moonmq/server.key" } is the minimum; add "CaFile" plus "Verify": "required" for mutual TLS (client certificates). Needs luasec. Each listener configures its own block: Server.Tls, Server.MetricsTls, Server.Cluster.Tls, Server.Replication.Tls. See docs/security.md.
Server._ChannelBinding_note: Server.Tls.ChannelBinding controls SCRAM channel binding (tls-server-end-point). "preferred" (the default) binds the SCRAM exchange to this listener's certificate whenever the client asks for it, and refuses a client that claims the broker cannot bind - which is how a stripped-TLS relay is caught. "required" refuses any SCRAM login that is not bound; "disabled" turns the offer off. SIGHUP revalidates and reloads every TLS listener's certificate without a restart. See docs/security.md.
Server._ClusterRaft_note: Server.Cluster.Raft turns cluster metadata into a replicated log: which broker is controller and which broker owns which partition are agreed by a majority instead of by a last-writer-wins file. { "Enabled": true } with the existing Server.Cluster.Peers is enough; ElectionTimeoutMs (2500), HeartbeatMs (500), RpcTimeoutMs (1000), CommitTimeoutSeconds (10) and MaxLogEntries (512) tune it. Omit the block and the broker keeps the epoch-fencing behaviour. See docs/cluster.md.
Server._MetricsTls_note: Same shape as Server.Tls, for the metrics port. Worth setting whenever MetricsAuth.Basic is on: Basic credentials over plaintext hand the scraper's password to anyone on the path.
Server._MetricsAuth_note: Credential gate on /metrics and /stats. Omit (the default) and they stay open, which is why MetricsHost defaults to loopback: /stats lists every topic name and its size on disk. { "Token": "..." } requires 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (also readable from the MOONMQ_METRICS_TOKEN env var, so it need not live in this file); { "Basic": true } accepts HTTP Basic against Auth.Users, requiring the cluster:describe permission. /health is always open. See docs/security.md.

Dlq._note: A record NACKed MaxDeliveries times by a consumer group is moved to <topic><Suffix> and the group advances past it. MaxDeliveries=1 dead-letters on the first NACK.

Replication._note: Single-leader replication. Role: leader|follower|both. A leader ships to Peers ([{Id,Address}]); a follower serves POST /replicate on ReplicatePort. Set Acks='all' to block produces until followers ack.
Replication._Tls_note: One block configures both halves of the link: the follower's /replicate listener and the leader's client to it, so it cannot end up encrypted in one direction only. Every record crosses this port.

Auth._PasswordHash_note: original password: admin. A lone Auth.Username is a SUPERUSER: it may produce to, consume from, and delete every topic. Generate a replacement with `make hash PASSWORD=... SCRAM=1`; the scram-sha-256 format is preferred because, unlike pbkdf2-sha256, it is not login-equivalent if this file leaks.
Auth._Users_note: Multi-tenancy. Replace the single Username above with a Users list, each entry { Username, PasswordHash, Superuser?, Acls?, Quota? }. Acls are { Resource: topic|group|cluster, Name: "orders.*"|"*", Operations: [read,write,create,delete,alter,describe] | "*", Effect: allow|deny } — default deny, and deny beats allow. A user with no Acls and no Superuser can authenticate but do nothing. Worked examples: docs/security.md.
Auth._Quotas_note: Token buckets, per principal and per topic. { "Default": {...}, "Topics": { "orders": {...} }, "BurstSeconds": 2 }; per-user limits live on the user entry above. Dimensions: RequestsPerSec, ProduceRecordsPerSec, ProduceBytesPerSec, FetchRecordsPerSec, FetchBytesPerSec. 0 means unlimited, and an all-zero block on a user opts it out of Default. Both the user and topic bucket must have room; request paths get ERR_RATE_LIMITED with a retry-after, the SUBSCRIBE push path is slowed instead.
